finite_deltas.old: hoc eodem sacramento quo nos temporaliter vegetas
finite_deltas.comparison: hoc eodem quo nos temporaliter vegetas sacramento

finite_deltas.meaning: graciously / as one who is gracious; modifier of the addressed giver

modern_expression_assessment.recommendation: qualified affirmative for this complete expression only, subject to independent review and Root decision
positive: One complete old prayer supplies the whole ordered expression: reception of the saving gift; appeal to divine mercy; the same sacrament sustaining present life; petition for participation in everlasting life. No new clause, image, actor, temporal relation, or requested result is introduced.

The two changes of position leave every dependency and proposition intact: sacramento remains the instrumental antecedent of quo; efficias still governs the same nos and participes. These are ordinary Latin ordering alternatives rather than a new expressive sequence assembled from disparate sources.

The sole added lexical item benignus is a conventional predicative adjective of the same addressed giver, rendered adverbially as graciously. The prayer already invokes that giver’s misericordia. It adds an ordinary polite qualification to the same act rather than a distinctive new description or theological proposition.

Assessed together, the ordering adjustments and this routine graciousness modifier do not create a recognizably new prayer expression beyond the complete old composition. The proposed narrow United States basis is the old whole work plus minor conventional editorial variations, not a claim that every word taken separately is free or that any short addition is automatically harmless.
strongest_contrary: The modern editor chose both the placement of the relative clause and a terminal cadence with benignus efficias. That coordinated rhetorical choice may be alleged to be original derivative authorship even though its ingredients are commonplace; the creativity threshold is low.

Benignus is an actual addition, not a spelling correction. No whole pre1931 witness containing the complete changed expression has been located in the declared search boundary. The modern edition supplied the comparison and cannot be concealed as an unused source.

An affirmative decision therefore depends on an individualized assessment that this exact configuration remains minor and conventional. It cannot establish a reusable rule for other additions, reordered clauses, or newly composed prayers.

Satiati munere salutari, tuam, Domine, misericordiam deprecamur, ut, hoc eodem quo nos temporaliter vegetas sacramento, perpetuae vitae participes benignus efficias.

rows.proposed_english:
Filled with the saving gift, Lord, we implore your mercy: through this very sacrament by which you sustain us in this life, graciously make us sharers in everlasting life.
Through Christ our Lord.
R. Amen.

english_fidelity_notes: Satiati is completed reception, not a request to be fed; saving gift retains munere salutari.

This very sacrament retains hoc eodem; by which and through preserve quo and the instrumental sacramento relation.
Sustain us in this life renders temporaliter vegetas without identifying the sacrament with ordinary food.
Graciously explicitly renders the reviewed benignus addition; sharers in everlasting life retains participes perpetuae vitae.

finite_deltas.meaning: old libamen denotes a sacramental draught/offering; modern alimonia emphasizes nourishment

modern_expression_assessment.recommendation: qualified affirmative for this complete expression only, subject to independent review and Root decision
positive: One complete old prayer supplies the entire sacramental-reception, appeal-to-clemency, repeated-celebration and redemptive-effect structure. The modern form does not juxtapose fragments from different prayers or add a new petition, actor, purpose, or theological result.

Alimonia replaces the ablative libamine in the same instrumental relation to renovati and the same genitive Body-and-Blood object. Nourishment and sacramental draught/offering are not identical lexical meanings; the difference is expressly retained in both the comparison and the new English.

Despite that lexical distinction, the replacement is an ordinary functional sacramental-food noun, not a newly fashioned image or phrase. Moving renovati after its instrument and gerimus before devotione frequenti does not change any semantic or syntactic dependency.

Assessed as one expression, the complete old prayer remains the expressive composition. The proposed narrow United States basis treats the commonplace noun replacement and ordinary ordering adjustments as minor editorial variations, while refusing to call them lexical identity or a pre1931 exact reading.
strongest_contrary: The deliberate move from libamen to alimonia can foreground nourishment instead of sacrificial draught/offering. That is a real editorial choice and may be argued to supply meaningful expressive variation rather than a merely mechanical correction.

The new word order and noun could be assessed together as a deliberate reshaping of a short liturgical composition. The low originality threshold makes a count-based argument insufficient, and the old whole source does not independently print the altered reading.

If the reviewer judges that sacramental nourishment is a distinctive new emphasis in this exact sentence rather than a conventional functional substitution, the complete modern-form candidate must remain held; the different old prayer cannot silently fill its slot.

rows.proposed_latin:
Sacri Corporis et Sanguinis pretiosi alimonia renovati, quaesumus, Domine, clementiam tuam, ut, quod gerimus devotione frequenti, certa redemptione capiamus.
Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
R. Amen.
rows.proposed_english:
Renewed by the nourishment of the sacred Body and precious Blood, we ask your kindness, Lord, that we may receive as sure redemption what we celebrate with frequent devotion.
Through Christ our Lord.
R. Amen.
rows.english_kind: Original project study translation; no approved or historical-human English source is claimed.
english_fidelity_notes: Renewed preserves renovati; by the nourishment explicitly renders alimonia rather than silently reverting to libamine.
Sacred Body and precious Blood preserve the two genitives and their attributes.
We ask your kindness renders quaesumus clementiam tuam as a request to the addressed Lord.
What we celebrate with frequent devotion retains the relative object and gerimus/devotione frequenti relation.
Receive as sure redemption is a deliberately close study rendering of certa redemptione capiamus; independent review must assess its English clarity and ablative relation.
